{"data":{"issue":{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","identifier":"TRK-1","title":"meta: Pod policy profiles: hands-on, standard, hands-off, autonomous, activatable per project","description":"## Where we are

Groomed on 2026-11-08 (PST) in keeper's coordination session on mini, hands-on route: grill round 1 page, all 12 answers the recommendation. 8 points, one xl Story with three Checkpoints, no child tickets. Not launched by the shop: S14b (TRK-2) runs it under Pod with `impl-xlarge@1` and the coordinator pair, the coordinator session as operator, keeper at the merge and `hqa_after_deploy` waits. Next: S14b launches once S14a and S15b (Done) and this ticket are ready; reread each Constraint against Pod `origin/main` at launch.

Size: xl on the tracker; 8 points

Proved: 10 callers, 0 fakes, 0 asserting tests, 6/6 checks fail today, origin/main 96d2999 2026-11-08

## Goal

As the operator, I want Pod to own the four policy profiles `hands-on`, `standard`, `hands-off`, and `autonomous`, activatable per project, so that the human gates of a project come from one named profile instead of hand-edited policy rows.

## Grill result

Grill round 1, answered 2026-11-08 by keeper, every answer option A (the recommendation): Q1 A, Q2 A, Q3 A, Q4 A, Q5 A, Q6 A, Q7 A, Q8 A, Q9 A, Q10 A, Q11 A, Q12 A (`recommended: true` on all 12).

* Q1: The four definitions live in the `profiles` block of `specs/policy/default.yaml`, a policy Revision. An adopter changes them in its own policy Revision. No new config kind.
* Q2: `hands-on` and `standard` lift no Gate. `hands-off` and `autonomous` lift `prd_review` and `design_clickthrough` to `decision-pair-aqa`. All four keep `hqa_after_deploy`, `staging_review`, and the HQA PR review with a person.
* Q3: A profile carries `deploy_production: needs_human | agent`. The global Reserved member stays; only the active profile, when it says `agent`, removes it. `droppedMember` is unchanged for an ordinary project policy.
* Q4: All four are defined. `hands-on`, `standard`, and `hands-off` can be activated. Activating `autonomous` still returns `gate_lift_refused`, with `next:` pointing at the TRK-3 spec section.
* Q5: A project activates a profile with a project-scope policy Revision that carries `active_profile: <name>`, applied with `pod config apply`. No new verb.
* Q6: `pod config apply` writes that Revision as pending. It takes effect only when `pod check` reads back a source-verified human tracker comment, such as `profile <project> <name>`, verified as S13b verifies a human ruling. `pod config apply` prints that comment text and never posts it.
* Q7: A switch during a live Run is accepted. A live Run keeps its pinned snapshot; the new profile applies from the next `pod run create`. The reply lists the Runs still on the old profile.
* Q8: `pod state` prints `Profile: <name> (policy <rev>)` in the policies section. `pod brief` prints one line per project and adds `profile` to its JSON. The Run snapshot records the profile name, and `pod brief` marks a Run whose snapshot profile differs from the current one.
* Q9: The process `profiles.json` and TRK-4's groom routing stay. A later process ticket removes them once Pod has a project profile and groom runs through Pod (TRK-5).
* Q10: Excluded: `attention` (`pause_at`, `max_unattended_hours`), the digest cap and per-project needs_human spec sections (TRK-6), TRK-7's gate set and needs-human exit, and step `method` override (TRK-3). This ticket adds only an activation Spec clarification to the tech spec's Gate-lift section.
* Q11: The S14b Run uses the global policy with no `active_profile` (the same as hands-on). After deploy, on the new build, the keeper applies `active_profile: hands-on` to the dogfood project, sees the profile line in `pod state`, then runs `hqa record`.
* Q12: One xl Story (stage impl, size xl) with three Checkpoints the planner takes as Tasks, not child tickets. keeper accepted this departure from the shop's rule that work over 3 points splits into children, so that S14b measures one real xl Run.

Added after the grill (keeper, 2026-11-08): every Run's config snapshot is kept in the database, and it records the active profile name.

## Constraints

* Policy definitions: `specs/policy/default.yaml` `profiles` holds four definitions, `hands-on`, `standard`, `hands-off`, `autonomous`, each with `replaces` per Q2 and `deploy_production` per Q3 (`needs_human` on the first three, `agent` on `autonomous`).
* Validation: `src/core/config/policy.ts` (`profileProblem`, `activeProfile`, `droppedMember`) accepts `deploy_production: needs_human | agent` on a profile, keeps the liftable set to `prd_review` and `design_clickthrough`, and refuses `active_profile` naming a profile the Revision does not define. `droppedMember` still refuses a project policy that drops a global deny or needs_human member.
* Activation: `src/core/config/apply.ts` `policyRefusal` stops refusing every `active_profile`. A project-scope policy Revision with `active_profile` set to `hands-on`, `standard`, or `hands-off` is recorded pending; `pod config apply` prints the comment a person posts and never posts it. `pod check` activates it only after reading back a source-verified human tracker comment, through the S13b ruling source rules (tech spec "accepted human source"). An agent-written apply never activates a profile by itself. `autonomous` stays `gate_lift_refused` with `next:` naming TRK-3's spec section.
* Consistency with TRK-8 (keeper's 2026-11-08 direction): the database is the source of configuration and `specs/` its mirror; an agent-written Revision is pending until a person activates it. This ticket implements that approval for `active_profile` only; it adds no `pod config set` verb, no `--activate` flag, no export, and no actor-from-identity change. It does not wait on TRK-8.
* Snapshot: `src/db/schema/config.ts` `config.snapshot` gains the profile name (nullable text, null when no profile is active), written by `pod run create` beside `policy_revision_id`, through a Drizzle-generated migration in `db/migrations/` (`0013_*`, ADR 0001). The snapshot row is never updated after it is pinned: a later activation changes neither the profile name nor the policy Revision id of an existing Run.
* Live Run switch: per Q7, a switch during a live Run is accepted, the live Run keeps its snapshot, and the reply lists the Runs still on the old profile. The tech spec fixture "a lift on a running Run is refused" still holds, because no running Run's Gates change.
* Surfaces: `pod state` (`src/core/state/sections.ts`, `src/core/state/render.ts`) prints `Profile: <name> (policy <rev>)` in the policies section; `pod brief` (`src/cli/brief.ts` and its JSON) carries `profile` per project and marks a Run whose snapshot profile differs from the current one. `docs/contract.md` documents both.
* Spec: `docs/tech-spec.md` Gate-lift section gains one `Spec clarification:` paragraph for activation (pending until the human readback, autonomous still refused, snapshot pins the profile). Row 8 of the conformance table ("every gate-lift activation is refused", line 1282) is reworded to the autonomous refusal and the out-of-set lift.
* Tests this ticket updates: `test/db/config-apply.test.ts` "active_profile is gate_lift_refused, naming a Run with unsettled Tasks" (line 927) changes to the pending path; `test/replay/gate-lift-refused.test.ts` (autonomous activation refused) stays green. New: `test/config/policy-profiles.test.ts` and `test/replay/profiles.test.ts` (both absent today; `test/config/` is a new directory), and `test/replay/profiles/` fixtures in the form of the other replays.
* Release: the PR carries the `package.json` patch bump that S14b's `pnpm deploy:host-a` needs.
* Pod code and tests stay free of shop names, hosts, people, bots, and providers; the scope scan passes.
* Guardrail: rung 4, blocks keeper, evidence TRK-9, TRK-10. A profile activation is a human confirmation.

## Completion check

* Checkpoint 1: `test -f test/config/policy-profiles.test.ts && pnpm -s vitest run test/config/policy-profiles.test.ts` passes, covering the four definitions, a lift outside `prd_review` and `design_clickthrough` refused, `deploy_production` per profile, and `autonomous` activation refused.
* Checkpoint 1: `test "$(grep -Ec "^    (hands-on|standard|hands-off|autonomous):" specs/policy/default.yaml)" = 4` exits 0.
* Checkpoint 2: `grep -q "profile" src/db/schema/config.ts && ls db/migrations/0013_*.sql` exits 0.
* Checkpoint 2: `grep -q "hands-on activation waits for the human readback" test/db/config-apply.test.ts && grep -q "a Run snapshot keeps its profile after a later activation" test/db/config-apply.test.ts && pnpm -s vitest run test/db/config-apply.test.ts` passes. The second case asserts that a Run created under an active profile records the profile name and the policy Revision id in `config.snapshot`, and that a later activation changes neither.
* Checkpoint 3: `test -f test/replay/profiles.test.ts && pnpm -s vitest run test/replay/profiles.test.ts` passes, with one replay per activatable profile, asserting the `pod brief` JSON `profile` and the `pod state` `Profile:` line.
* Checkpoint 3: `sed -n "/^#### Gate-lift/,/^#### Decision measurement/p" docs/tech-spec.md | grep -q "Spec clarification"` exits 0.
* On the final head: `pnpm -s vitest run` passes, the scope scan passes, `package.json` carries a patch bump over 96d2999's `0.1.0`, and the PR body pairs each item here with its result.
* After the merge and deploy, owner keeper (HQA after deploy, in S14b): on the new build, apply `active_profile: hands-on` to the dogfood project, post the readback comment, and see `Profile: hands-on (policy <rev>)` in `pod state`, then `hqa record`.

## Exclusions

* No `attention` (`pause_at`, `max_unattended_hours`).
* No TRK-6 spec sections (digest cap, per-project needs_human), no TRK-7 gate set, no TRK-3 `replaces`/`requires` table or step `method` override; `autonomous` activation stays refused.
* No `pod config set`, `--activate`, `pod config export`, or actor-from-identity work (TRK-8).
* No `pod policy` verb (TRK-10 follow-up).
* No change to the process repo's `profiles.json` or groom routing (TRK-4); Q9 files that later.
* No child tickets.

## Source and links

* Source of truth: grill round 1 page [https://claude.ai/artifact/NKQgGnqmS4qKe31sMVnCxB](<https://claude.ai/artifact/NKQgGnqmS4qKe31sMVnCxB>) with answers recorded under Grill result; Pod `origin/main` 96d2999; tech spec "Policy schema" and "Gate-lift" (`docs/tech-spec.md` line 1109).
* Story: none
* Epic: TRK-11
* Run by: TRK-2 (S14b) under TRK-12 (S14); this ticket blocks TRK-2.
* Related: TRK-8 (database is the source of configuration; generalizes this ticket's human activation; not a blocker), TRK-9 (profiles grill), TRK-4 (process profiles.json), TRK-10 (S13 policy schema), TRK-3, TRK-6, TRK-7, TRK-5.
* Ordering notes from the overlap check: `docs/tech-spec.md` is also named by TRK-12, TRK-2, and TRK-13 (Todo); `docs/contract.md` by TRK-13; `package.json` by TRK-2.
* PRD: none
* Design: none
* Milestone: none

## Gates

| Gate | Type | Gatekeeper | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Tech design review | AQA | crew (reviewer) | pending |
| PR review | AQA | crew (reviewer) | pending |
| HQA PR review | HQA | keeper | pending |
| HQA after deploy | HQA | keeper | pending |

Tech design review is pending because the change alters the policy `profiles` schema, adds a human activation path, and adds a snapshot column. The merge waits on the crew PR review PASS and keeper's HQA PR review PASS (epic rule). HQA after deploy is a real human wait (Q11): after deploy, one `pod` verb on the new build activates hands-on.

## Checkpoints

- [ ] Rules: the four profile definitions, `deploy_production` per profile, and validation (`specs/policy/default.yaml`, `src/core/config/policy.ts`, `test/config/policy-profiles.test.ts`)
- [ ] Activation: pending apply, human readback through `pod check`, snapshot profile column and migration, live-Run switch (`src/core/config/apply.ts`, `src/db/schema/config.ts`, `db/migrations/0013_*`, `test/db/config-apply.test.ts`)
- [ ] Surfaces and proof: `pod state` and `pod brief` profile lines, one replay per activatable profile, `docs/contract.md`, the Gate-lift Spec clarification, `package.json` patch bump (`test/replay/profiles.test.ts`)

## Kickoff

Kickoff: impl-xlarge@1

Run by Pod, not launched with `trk-process kickoff`: S14b (TRK-2) runs `pod run create` for this ticket with the shipped `impl-xlarge@1` and the coordinator pair, and Pod reads the line above as the process name.
